segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon beneath her feet and on her head a crown of twelve stars.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She was pregnant, and she was crying out in labor pains, in agony to give birth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And another sign appeared in heaven—and look, a great fiery-red dragon, with seven heads and ten horns, and on his heads seven diadems.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His tail dragged a third of the stars of the sky and hurled them to the earth. And the dragon stood in front of the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she gave birth he might devour her child.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: She gave birth to a son, a male child, who is going to shepherd all the nations with an iron rod. And her child was snatched away to God and to his throne.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, so that there she might be nourished for one thousand two hundred and sixty days.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels made war on the dragon. The dragon and his angels made war,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but he did not prevail, and no place was found for them in heaven any longer.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the great dragon was hurled down—the ancient serpent, who is called the Devil and Satan, the one who leads the whole inhabited world astray—he was hurled to the earth, and his angels were hurled down with him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And I heard a loud voice in heaven saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Now the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God and the authority of his Christ have come, because the accuser of our brothers and sisters has been hurled down, the one who accuses them before our God day and night.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And they conquered him because of the blood of the Lamb and because of the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives even to the point of death.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Therefore rejoice, you heavens and you who dwell in them! Woe to the earth and the sea, because the Devil has come down to you in great fury, knowing that he has only a short time.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when the dragon saw that he had been hurled to the earth, he pursued the woman who had given birth to the male child.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the woman was given the two wings of the great eagle, so that she might fly into the wilderness, to her place, where she is nourished for a time and times and half a time, away from the presence of the serpent.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the serpent hurled water like a river from his mouth after the woman, to have her carried off by the river.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the earth came to the woman’s help: the earth opened its mouth and swallowed the river that the dragon had hurled from his mouth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the dragon was enraged at the woman and went off to make war on the rest of her offspring, those who keep God’s commandments and hold the testimony of Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he stood on the sand of the sea.

notes.note: The Greek word meant a huge serpent or sea monster, not the winged, fire-breathing creature of later European legend. In the Greek Old Testament it is used for Leviathan and for the chaos monsters that stand for powers hostile to God, such as Pharaoh's Egypt. Verse 9 identifies this one with the serpent of Genesis.

This is a different word from the 'crown' of verse 1. That word denotes a wreath of victory or honor; this one is the band worn by a king as the emblem of sovereignty. The dragon's seven diadems are a claim to royal rule.

This is the same Greek word translated 'heaven' elsewhere in the chapter; it covers both the visible sky and the dwelling of God. 'Sky' is used here because the stars are in view. In a vision like this the two senses are not sharply separated.

The verb means to tend a flock and, by extension, to govern. The phrase echoes Psalm 2:9 in its Greek form, which has 'shepherd them with an iron rod' where the Hebrew as traditionally read has 'break them'. Most translations render 'rule'; 'shepherd' keeps the image, in which the rod is the herdsman's club. Some scholars think the context of the psalm gives the verb a harsher sense here, closer to 'crush'.

The Greek word is the one translated 'Gentiles' elsewhere in the New Testament where it means the non-Jewish peoples. It is rendered 'nations' here, as usual in Revelation, because the scope is every people of the world.

notes.phrase: one thousand two hundred and sixty days
notes.note: This equals forty-two months of thirty days, or three and a half years. It is the same period as the 'time and times and half a time' of verse 14, a phrase taken from Daniel 7:25 and 12:7, where it marks a limited period of persecution of God's people.

The Greek word was an ordinary term for a slanderer or false accuser. The Greek Old Testament uses it to translate the Hebrew 'satan', an adversary or accuser, as in the opening of Job. The original audience would have heard that meaning, and verse 10 picks it up by calling him 'the accuser'.

notes.traditional: by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony
notes.note: Most translations have 'by', which presents the blood and the testimony as the means of victory. The Greek construction (this preposition with the accusative case) normally gives the ground or reason: 'because of', 'on account of'. The difference is slight, and some scholars think the construction here does shade toward means.

The verb means both to chase and to persecute, and older translations have 'persecuted'. The narrative of flight in verses 14 to 16 favors 'pursued'. A reader in a persecuted church would have heard both senses.

notes.phrase: the two wings of the great eagle
notes.note: The image recalls the exodus, where God tells Israel, 'I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself' (Exodus 19:4; compare Deuteronomy 32:11). The woman's flight into the wilderness, where she is fed, follows the same pattern of rescue and provision.

The word is literally 'seed', and it echoes Genesis 3:15, where God puts enmity between the serpent and the woman, and between his seed and hers. Having called the dragon 'the ancient serpent' in verse 9, the chapter shows that enmity carried on against the woman's other children.

The Greek can mean the testimony Jesus himself bore, which his followers hold on to, or their testimony about Jesus. Scholars are divided, and the phrase recurs elsewhere in Revelation with the same ambiguity. The translation leaves it open, as the Greek does.

notes.traditional: I stood upon the sand of the sea
notes.note: The earliest manuscripts read 'he stood', meaning the dragon, who takes up a position on the shore before the beast rises from the sea. Many later manuscripts read 'I stood', which makes John the subject; the two forms differ by one letter. Older translations follow the later reading and attach the sentence to 13:1, and some modern editions number it 13:1 as well.

candidates.reason: A key verb in Revelation and the Johannine letters that translations split between 'overcome', 'conquer' and 'be victorious'; readers should see one word.
Recurs across John, Acts and Revelation with 'testimony' and 'witness' both in common use, and the related noun for a witness shades toward 'martyr' in Revelation.
The plural for members of the community occurs throughout the New Testament and translations vary between 'brothers', 'brethren', 'brothers and sisters' and 'believers'.
The split between 'life' and 'soul' needs one policy, since 'soul' often misleads a modern reader where the life or the self is meant.
The choice between 'kingdom', 'reign' and 'kingship' recurs in every part of the New Testament and should be decided once if the register does not already cover it.
